subject: Legal hold interplay with backups and GDPR — guidance and next steps

Subject: Clarification on legal hold for backups & GDPR

Hi Alex —

We're opening an internal review triggered by a regulatory inquiry and need to understand how Redwood handles legal holds relative to backups and immutable snapshots. A few specific asks:

- Can HealOps request an account-level legal hold that permanently prevents deletion of backups, logs, and prompt cache for a particular customer?
- Are immutable snapshots treated differently (i.e., can Redwood exclude snapshots from normal TTL/auto-purge while a hold is active)?
- Practical timelines: if we issue a legal hold today, how quickly can you suspend scheduled purges (logs, backups, prompt cache)?
- Does Redwood provide a chain-of-custody/manifest for snapshots and backups (hashes, creation times) suitable for auditors?

Please point us to the form/process and any evidence you can share (SOC 2 excerpt, manifest example). If easier, happy to schedule a short call.

Thanks,
Jenna Ortiz

On 2028-10-01 09:12, Jenna Ortiz wrote:
> We're opening an internal review... Can HealOps request an account-level legal hold that permanently prevents deletion of backups, logs, and prompt cache for a particular customer?

Short answers up front: yes with caveats. Details below.

1) What we can do today
- Account-level hold: We support an account-level "preserve" flag that suspends scheduled retention-driven purges for object stores, snapshot pipelines, and the centralized log TTL manager. When active, automated deletion jobs skip objects tagged with the hold ID.
- Immutable snapshots: Snapshots created as "immutable" (WORM-style) are not subject to rolling deletion. We can elevate a snapshot to immutable on request, provided the snapshot hasn't already been garbage-collected.
- Prompt cache vs. user-supplied content: Prompt KV caches and ephemeral prompt artifacts are normally retained for a short default window (config: 30 days). Holds can extend that window, but we treat model input/outputs and customer-provided data separately for compliance labeling.

2) Timelines and operational constraints
- Suspension latency: From the time we receive an approved legal hold form and verify requester authority, we can block scheduled purge jobs within 48 hours. For immediate incidents we can initiate an expedited manual suspension (same business day) but it requires SOC approval.
- Snapshot promotion: If you ask us to promote an existing snapshot to immutable, that operation is typically immediate (under 1 hour) if the snapshot is present. If the snapshot has been expired by a prior job, we cannot recover it unless there is an existing archived copy.
- Retention extension windows: We can set extension windows of indefinite length while the hold is active, but permanent deletion policies still apply to certain low-level append-only audit logs that are managed under separate retention contracts — we'll flag any exceptions in the manifest.

3) Evidence and chain of custody
- We can provide a snapshot manifest CSV containing object ids, creation timestamps, SHA256 checksums, storage regions, and the job id that produced the snapshot. Example attached: snapshot_manifest_20281001.csv (redacted).
- We maintain an audit trail for all hold toggles (who requested, approver, timestamp) and can export a signed event log for auditors.

4) Legal/process
- Formal process: we require a completed legal_hold_request_form.pdf (attached) plus an authorized signatory and PO or support ticket ID. Our legal team must approve the request for holds longer than 90 days or any request that overrides contractual deletion obligations.

Caveats:
- Backups stored in cold-archive with a third-party provider have separate retention constraints; we can coordinate a hold but lead times may be longer (up to 7 business days).
- If a court order mandates preservation across multiple customers or broader scope, our Legal team will request clarifying scope and may require an escrow/fee to cover extended storage costs.

Attachments: snapshot_manifest_20281001.csv

Let me know if you want the SOC 2 summary while we start intake; Alex/Grace can coordinate an intake checklist and call.

Thanks,

Hi Jenna —

Thanks for raising this. Pragmatic next steps from Customer Success/legal intake perspective (proposed MAP):

1) HealOps completes the legal_hold_request_form.pdf and returns with an authorized signatory + brief scope (customer id, time window, specific artifacts to preserve).
2) Redwood Security (Soojin) will verify snapshot availability and provide snapshot_manifest_20281001.csv and an estimate for any archive retrieval times.
3) Redwood Legal receives the form and issues approval or follow-up questions within 48 business hours for standard holds; for extended holds (>90 days) Legal will send a confirmation and cost estimate.
4) We place the preserve flag (or promote snapshot to immutable) within 48 hours of Legal approval and notify HealOps with the signed event log.
5) Redwood will deliver an initial evidence package (manifest + SOC 2 summary redacted) to your DPO and our audit contact.

If that workflow looks good we can convert this thread into a support/intake ticket and schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the form together.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor

Thanks, Grace and team.

This is helpful. Two quick follow-ups before we start intake:
- Can you confirm whether the SOC 2 summary redacted contains the change-control logs for snapshot promotions and holds? Our auditors want to see evidence that hold toggles are covered by change-control narratives.
- For chain of custody, will the manifest include signed hashes (SHA256) and a signed timestamp (we use RFC-3161 style time-stamping for audits)?

Michael (copied) is our external counsel and will be coordinating the legal sign-off. If you can attach the SOC 2 excerpt and the sample signed manifest in this thread that will speed our review.

Cheers,
Jenna
